articles.title: The Ethics of Voice Cloning: What Developers Should Know

articles.body: Why Ethics Matter in Voice Cloning Voice cloning is no longer a niche research project—it's a mainstream product feature in virtual assistants, gaming, and customer support. Every line of synthesized speech feels natural because the models have learned the nuances of human prosody, tone, and accent. As developers, we’re excited to build experiences that “talk” like us, but with great power comes great responsibility. Ignoring the ethical implications can lead to legal trouble, brand damage, and, more importantly, loss of trust. Below, we’ll walk through the key ethical concerns, how they intersect with the technology stack you’re building, and practical steps you can take to stay compliant and respectful. 1. Consent: The Foundation of Ethical Voice Cloning What Is Consent in This Context?

articles.body: I went looking for one thing, failed to find it, and measured something more useful on the way. Both results are below, including the hypothesis that did not survive. The setup 60 specific products across ten categories: graded cards, retro games, sneakers, watches, lenses, coins, tools, collectibles, consumer electronics. For each one, the same query twice, once over 90 days and once over 1,095 days, reading cleaned server side statistics rather than raw listings. 120 requests, paced. The question: eBay's public sold filter shows about 90 days. How much of an item's sales record does that window hide? The hypothesis failed I expected thin 90 day windows and rich three year ones. Instead, 58 of 59 comparable queries already had eight or more clean sales inside 90 days .

articles.body: If your Node.js code reads Google's daily trending searches with google-trends-api , it probably fails like this now: SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!doctype "... is not valid JSON The call itself does not throw. googleTrends.dailyTrends({ geo: 'US' }) resolves, but what it resolves with is Google's HTML "404 Not Found" page, and your JSON.parse chokes on the first < . In Python, pytrends has the same problem with a clearer message: ResponseError: The request failed: Google returned a response with code 404 . This post shows what still works, what does not, and how to get the trending searches for any list of countries, with search volume and news links, from Node.js or Python with one API call.

articles.title: Why You Should Keep a Decision Log (and a Simple Format to Start With)
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: this post was written with AI assistance and reviewed before publishing. Six months after an important decision, most teams can tell you what they decided but not why. The context — the op…
articles.body: Disclosure: this post was written with AI assistance and reviewed before publishing. Six months after an important decision, most teams can tell you what they decided but not why . The context — the options considered, the constraints at the time, the assumptions — disappears. A decision log is a lightweight way to keep it. It's useful for teams and solo founders alike, and it takes a couple of minutes per decision. What a decision log gives you Memory. New team members can understand why things are the way they are. Fewer repeated debates. When someone asks "why don't we just…?", you can point to the entry, and reopen it only if something has changed. Better judgement over time. Reviewing past decisions against outcomes shows where your reasoning tends to be good or weak.

articles.body: A public n8n issue describes a webhook workflow that has already returned a successful HTML response while its execution, which includes a PostgreSQL node, still shows as running. We cannot diagnose or fix that vendor issue, and we do not represent anyone affected by it. It does raise an adjacent question for teams building identity onboarding. When the HTTP layer says done but the work behind it has not finished, what should your application believe about a verification session? This article answers that question with the synthetic verification_delivery fixture. The goal is to help you decide whether a sandbox integration fits your task. The problem and your decision A 200 response tells the sender only that a request was received.

articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. 3D 67P Explanation: Put on your red/blue glasses and float next to the jagged and double-lobed nucleus of Churyumov-Gerasimenko, also known as Comet 67P . The stereo anaglyph was created by combining two images from the Rosetta spacecraft’s narrow angle OSIRIS camera taken on July 25, 2015 from a distance of 184 kilometers. Numerous jets are emanating from the small solar system world’s active surface near its closest approach to the Sun.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
